title: feat: move Kimi K3 to Fireworks
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes `kimi-k3` to Fireworks standard serverless with no fallback.
- Keeps the existing model contract and $3/M input, $0.30/M cached-input, and $15/M output pricing.
- Opens the model to Quest Pollen while retaining multiplier 1.
- Verifies text, vision (1/10 images), reasoning, tools, JSON, streaming, prompt cache, billing, errors, and 5/15/30-request bursts end to end.
- Passes Gen tests/typecheck and focused Enter registry, access, and effective-price tests (302/302).

gist.headline: Kimi found a new launchpad
gist.blurb: Kimi K3 has moved to Fireworks and kept its whole toolkit packed neatly in the basket. Text, vision, tools, streaming, reasoning, and cached prompts are all still buzzing along.
gist.summary: Routed kimi-k3 to Fireworks standard serverless without fallback while preserving its existing API contract, $3/M input, $0.30/M cached-input, and $15/M output pricing, and enabling Quest Pollen access at multiplier 1.
gist.impact: Developers can keep using kimi-k3 for text, vision, reasoning, tools, JSON, streaming, and prompt caching at the same prices, now backed by Fireworks and available through Quest Pollen.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-migration scene: Polli helps a friendly Kimi K3 code capsule board a small Fireworks-powered serverless rocket at a garden launchpad, while a CRT monitor robot confirms that text, vision, tools, JSON, and streaming cargo are all accounted for. Flowering code-plants and labeled prompt-cache crates represent the preserved contract and capabilities.
